clue.text: Clear off, having swallowed English breakfast food

indicators.note: something that has swallowed another thing holds it inside, so one piece goes within the other
off in the sense of gone wrong or bad, telling us the letters of the word before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone is told to clear off after gobbling down a full English breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' scrambles CLEAR to CERAL, and 'having swallowed' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornflakes and muesli are grain-based foods eaten in the morning with milk.

clue.text: Cold baskets for sparkling wine

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
hampers are wicker baskets, often for picnic food

explanation.surface: Chilled picnic baskets packed with bottles of fizz.
explanation.definitionFit: A British informal word for champagne, the best-known fizzy wine.

clue.text: Salesman allowed charge for fullness from eating

parts.note: a rep is a travelling sales representative
let means permitted or allowed
an ion is an atom carrying an electrical charge

explanation.surface: A salesman is permitted to bill for the state of being stuffed after a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' looks like a fee, but it is the electrical charge of an ion.
explanation.definitionFit: Being completely full or sated after a big meal.

clue.text: First man to have an apple?

definitions.text: First man to have an apple?

parts.words: First man to have an apple?
parts.note: the biblical first man ate the forbidden fruit, and the throat bulge named after him is a man's apple

explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the first man shared the forbidden fruit, and the larynx bulge carries his name.

clue.text: Bamboozle some, including Frenchman, making soup

parts.note: to con is to trick or bamboozle

indicators.note: one word including another holds it inside

parts.note: M is the abbreviation of Monsieur, a French man

explanation.surface: A Frenchman cons a few people into making soup.
explanation.definitionFit: A clear broth made from meat stock, served as a starter.

clue.text: Residence roofless, letter unfinished, but there's food

indicators.note: in a down clue the roof is the top letter, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a home is a residence

indicators.note: a word left unfinished has its last letter cut off

explanation.surface: A house without a roof and a half-written letter, but at least there is something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roofless' takes H off HOME to leave OME; 'unfinished' takes R off LETTER to leave LETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish of beaten eggs cooked in a pan, often folded around a filling.

clue.text: Lacking money for rich biscuit

parts.note: short of something means lacking it
bread is slang for money

explanation.surface: Being short of cash for an expensive biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: Shortbread is a buttery Scottish biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A crumbly Scottish biscuit made with lots of butter, hence rich.

clue.text: Fruit gives chap energy

parts.note: a chap is a man
go means energy or drive, as in full of go

explanation.surface: Eating fruit gives a fellow some pep.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical stone fruit with sweet orange flesh.

clue.text: The Spanish even have time for refreshments

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
taken as written

explanation.surface: Spaniards even make time for a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain elevenses is a mid-morning snack taken around eleven o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Mid-morning, the hour of the British snack break called elevenses.

clue.text: Sort of jelly, a flavouring almost

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: spice is a flavouring

explanation.surface: Something like a jelly, nearly a seasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops E from SPICE to leave SPIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A savoury gelatine made from meat stock, used to set cold dishes.

clue.text: Turns up with a soft fruit

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical abbreviation for soft
pears are a fruit

explanation.surface: Someone arrives bearing squishy fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soft fruit' looks like berries, but 'soft' gives P on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn up is to arrive or show oneself, i.e. come into view.

clue.text: Formally pronounce units of measurement and weight

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit for measuring type width
an ounce is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: An official reading out of units and weights.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter or proclaim words clearly, in a formal manner.

clue.text: Take skin off fish, quietly first

indicators.note: first says the piece just before it goes at the front

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical abbreviation for quietly
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: Instructions to skin a fish, doing it quietly first.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove the outer rind or skin of fruit or vegetables.

clue.text: Sent in more to be cooked for soup

indicators.note: food cooked is changed in form, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: More ingredients are sent in for the soup pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick Italian vegetable broth, often with pasta.

clue.text: One who samples drink with ten waiters (drunk)

indicators.note: drunk people are disordered, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone sampling the booze along with ten tipsy waiters.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional who tastes and judges vintages.

clue.text: Dried fruit is appearing during wet weather

indicators.note: something appearing during another is set in the middle of it

parts.note: rain is wet weather

explanation.surface: Dried fruit turns up when it is raining.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried grape, eaten as a snack or in cakes.

clue.text: First course on Saturday is more bitter

parts.note: S is a short form for Saturday
tarter means sharper or more bitter

explanation.surface: The opening dish served at the weekend is sharper than usual.
explanation.definitionFit: The appetiser served before the main dish.

clue.text: To recent fudge add English beefsteak

indicators.note: to fudge is to fiddle or muddle, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Add something English to a recent fudge recipe and you get a steak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fudge' rearranges TO RECENT to ENTRECOT, and E is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A boneless cut of beef from between the ribs.

clue.text: Get undressed elsewhere to remove working parts

parts.note: to strip is to take one's clothes off
out means away, not here

explanation.surface: Taking off clothes somewhere else.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismantle a machine and take out its components.

clue.text: At do, Cava replaced liqueur

indicators.note: letters replaced are put in new places, so the order changes

explanation.surface: At a party, Spanish sparkling wine was swapped for something sweeter.
explanation.walkthrough: Cava is a Spanish sparkling wine; advocaat is a Dutch egg liqueur.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick Dutch spirit made with eggs and brandy.

clue.text: Eats in with non-U visitors

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: non-U means without the letter U, so it is removed

parts.note: guests are visitors

explanation.surface: Dining at home with guests who are not upper class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-U' is also a British term for lower-class manners; here it drops U from GUESTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Swallows food, takes it into the body.

clue.text: Moistened while cooking half of repast in bed

indicators.note: one piece goes in the middle of the other

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: half of a word is one of its two halves, here the back three letters

explanation.surface: Eating half a meal in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Spooning fat or juices over meat during roasting.

clue.text: Advertise big meal

definitions.meaning: to advertise is to publicise or broadcast news widely
a lavish feast laid out on a table

explanation.definitionFit: Publicise widely; and a generous array of food laid on a table.

clue.text: Place a note in dish

parts.note: Pl. is the abbreviation for Place in street names
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Set a note down in a bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat piece of crockery for serving food.

clue.text: Audibly select a flowering plant for pickle

indicators.note: audibly means said out loud, so the phrase is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: select is pick, and a flowering plant is a lily

explanation.surface: Choosing a flower for the jar.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright yellow British relish of chopped vegetables in mustard.

clue.text: Leaders haven't got independent cooks

indicators.note: what they haven't got is taken away

parts.note: chiefs are leaders

explanation.surface: Bosses without independence are just cooks.
explanation.definitionFit: Professional cooks in a kitchen.

clue.text: Ban some of the native tomato growers

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the words are taken, a run inside them

explanation.surface: Banning some of those who grow local tomatoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A veto is a prohibition or refusal to allow something.

clue.text: Vegetable found in guest's pudding

indicators.note: the letters are found in a run across the words

explanation.surface: A vegetable turns up inside a visitor's dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal word for a potato.

clue.text: Choose or put back this sort of plate

parts.note: to elect is to choose

indicators.note: put back means the word is turned to run the other way

explanation.surface: Choose or swap back this type of plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' turns OR into RO. Electroplate is metal coated by electrolysis.
explanation.definitionFit: Prefix forming electroplate, metal coated using electric current.

clue.text: Cook a topical (but not large) pudding

indicators.note: to cook is to doctor or falsify, so the letters are reworked
but not says the following thing is left out

explanation.surface: Make a dessert that is topical but not large.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not' drops L from TOPICAL, and 'Cook' rearranges the remaining TOPICA to TAPIOC, with A added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A milky dessert made from cassava starch pearls.

clue.text: Separate dieters agitated about cook initially

indicators.note: about means around, one piece wrapping the other
agitated means stirred up, so these letters are rearranged
initially points to the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Dieters in a lather about the cook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitated' rearranges DIETERS to DISRETE, and 'about' wraps it round C.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinct and individually separate, not continuous.

clue.text: Publicity on opening is coming

parts.note: an ad is publicity
a vent is an opening

explanation.surface: An advert on a vent.
explanation.definitionFit: The arrival of something notable.
